item.title: Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
item.description:
Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant

Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that Russian embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

“Neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr nuclear power plant have any plans to evacuate. Work continues as normal,” the embassy said in a statement, dismissing reports to the contrary as “FAKES”.

Bushehr, Iran’s only operating nuclear power plant, has come under repeated attack during the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Satellite imagery released in July showed damage inside the complex.

Iran’s supreme leader directs judiciary to pursue US-Israeli war reparations
item.description:
Iran’s supreme leader directs judiciary to pursue US-Israeli war reparations

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has directed the judiciary to pursue compensation for "material and moral" damages caused by US-Israeli war, state news agency IRNA reported.

Khamenei issued the directive during a meeting with judiciary chief Gholam Hossein Mohseni Ejei, calling for the authorities to pursue the Iranian nation’s rights.

He also urged the judiciary to step up its fight against corruption, address its underlying causes and accelerate the handling of cases, with timely enforcement of rulings to serve as a deterrent.

item.title: Iran speaker to skip Delhi Brics meet due to 'unforeseen circumstances'
item.description:
Iran speaker to skip Delhi Brics meet due to 'unforeseen circumstances'

Iranian Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf will not attend the Brics parliamentary forum in New Delhi due to "certain unforeseen circumstances",  the Iranian embassy in India said on X.

Qalibaf was scheduled to attend the Meeting of Speakers of the parliaments of Brics member countries. 

The embassy said an Iranian parliamentary delegation would participate in the meeting, adding that Iran, as a Brics member, “reaffirms its commitment to active and effective participation at the highest levels in the summits and meetings of this grouping”.

Statement by the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in New Delhi Regarding the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum (24 October 2026) The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in New Delhi wishes to inform that, due to certain unforeseen circumstances, H.E. Dr. Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, will be unable to attend the Meeting of Speakers of the Parliaments of BRICS Member Countries in New Delhi. It is also emphasized that the parliamentary delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran will participate in the meeting. As one of the members of BRICS, Iran reaffirms its commitment to active and effective participation at the highest levels in the summits and meetings of this grouping. In this regard, the Iranian delegation will continue its dialogue and consultations with delegations from BRICS member countries, with a view to expanding and deepening bilateral and multilateral cooperation, particularly in the field of parliamentary relations and cooperation. The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran also expresses its sincere appreciation to the Government of the Republic of India for its gracious hospitality and the arrangements made to host this meeting. It wishes the Meeting of Speakers of the Parliaments of BRICS Member Countries every success and hopes that it will yield constructive outcomes towards strengthening cooperation and engagement among member countries.

— Iran in India (@Iran_in_India) October 24, 2026

item.title: Iraq says no US troops left in the country, not even advisers
item.description: Iraq’s prime minister said Friday that no US troops are left in the country, including in advisory roles, as Baghdad moves to bring all weapons under state control by next June, Anadolu reports. Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the absence of foreign forces had removed the justification armed factions previously cited for retaining their weapons. He stressed that the government’s decision to restrict weapons to state institutions was final and irreversible. “By June 30, 2027, there will be no weapons outside the framework of the state,” he said.
